root_cause.text: A race in `wm97xx_bat_probe()` registered the charger IRQ before the `bat_psy` power_supply object was allocated/registered, allowing `wm97xx_chrg_irq`/`wm97xx_bat_update()` to call `power_supply_changed()` on an uninitialized `bat_psy` pointer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `request_irq(gpiod_to_irq(charge_gpiod), wm97xx_chrg_irq, ...)` from before `power_supply_register()` to after it, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that an interrupt between `request_irq()` and `power_supply_register()` causes the `power_supply` handle to be used uninitialized, leading to a NULL pointer dereference.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop requesting the charge GPIO IRQ during battery probe so probing no longer depends on that interrupt registration.
intent_record.what: The code removes the request_irq() call for the charge_gpiod interrupt, along with its error handling and early return, from wm97xx_bat_probe() while keeping the GPIO consumer name assignment and property count increment intact.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the probe function no longer registers wm97xx_chrg_irq as an interrupt handler for the charge GPIO and will not fail probing if that IRQ request would have failed. The charge GPIO can still contribute the STATUS property, but charge-state change interrupts from this GPIO will no longer be handled here.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify `wm97xx_bat_probe()` allocation failure handling by returning `-ENOMEM` directly instead of jumping to the common error path.
intent_record.what: The allocation failure handling after `kcalloc(props, sizeof(*prop), GFP_KERNEL)` was changed from a braced `if (!prop)` block that assigned `ret = -ENOMEM` and jumped to `err3`, to a direct early return `if (!prop) return -ENOMEM;`.
intent_record.how: On memory allocation failure, the function now exits immediately with `-ENOMEM` instead of routing through the `err3` cleanup path, simplifying control flow and avoiding use of the shared error label for this case.

intent_record.intent_summary: Request the charge-detect GPIO IRQ during probe and fix cleanup so failed IRQ setup properly unregisters the power supply and frees resources.
intent_record.what: The error path in wm97xx_bat_probe() was changed so that failure after power_supply registration now jumps to a new free label instead of err4, and a new conditional block was added to request an IRQ for charge_gpiod using request_irq(gpiod_to_irq(charge_gpiod), wm97xx_chrg_irq, 0, "AC Detect", dev). If that IRQ request fails, the code logs the error with dev_err_probe(), jumps to a new unregister label, unregisters bat_psy with power_supply_unregister(), then falls through to free allocated prop memory with kfree(prop). The old err3/err4 cleanup path that conditionally called free_irq() was removed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the driver now actually registers the AC-detect/charge GPIO interrupt when charge_gpiod is present, enabling wm97xx_chrg_irq to be invoked on that IRQ. If IRQ setup fails after the power supply has already been registered, the probe now correctly unregisters the power supply and frees memory instead of leaving a partially initialized device. Removing free_irq() from the probe error path also avoids attempting to free an IRQ that was never successfully requested in the old flow.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant probe ordering is visible in this snippet, so the code is sufficient to judge the race. In `wm97xx_bat_probe()`, when `charge_gpiod` exists, the driver calls `request_irq(gpiod_to_irq(charge_gpiod), wm97xx_chrg_irq, 0, "AC Detect", dev);` before the power supply object is allocated/registered. Later in the same function, the code proceeds to set up properties and eventually registers the battery power supply (`bat_psy`), as shown by the later cleanup path `power_supply_unregister(bat_psy);` in remove and the probe error path labels after property setup. The root cause says the bug is registering the charger IRQ before `bat_psy` is allocated/registered, allowing `wm97xx_chrg_irq`/`wm97xx_bat_update()` to reach `power_supply_changed()` on an uninitialized `bat_psy`. This commit still has that vulnerable ordering: IRQ registration happens early, and no guard is shown preventing the IRQ handler/work from using `bat_psy` before registration. The GPIO descriptor conversion only changes GPIO handling (`devm_gpiod_get_optional`, `gpiod_to_irq`, `gpiod_get_value`) and does not move IRQ registration after power-supply registration or add any synchronization/NULL check fix for `bat_psy`.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it shows the ordering between IRQ registration and power_supply setup/registration. The vulnerable construct is present: at lines 196-198 the code calls `request_irq(gpio_to_irq(pdata->charge_gpio), wm97xx_chrg_irq, IRQF_DISABLED, "AC Detect", 0);` before the battery power_supply is fully initialized and registered. The `bat_ps` object is only populated later at lines 239-245 (`bat_ps.name`, `bat_ps.properties`, `bat_ps.num_properties`) and registered at line 246 with `power_supply_register(&dev->dev, &bat_ps)`. Per the root cause, registering the charger IRQ first allows `wm97xx_chrg_irq`/`wm97xx_bat_update()` to run and call `power_supply_changed()` before `bat_psy` is allocated/registered. There is no visible protection here preventing that race, and the fix would require delaying IRQ registration until after the power_supply object is allocated/registered. Therefore this version contains the bug and does not yet contain the fix.

The vulnerable construct is present: at lines 198-200 the code calls `request_irq(gpio_to_irq(pdata->charge_gpio), wm97xx_chrg_irq, 0, "AC Detect", dev);` before the power supply object is initialized and registered. The `bat_ps` fields are only assigned later at lines 241-246 (`bat_ps.name`, `bat_ps.properties`, `bat_ps.num_properties`), and the actual registration happens even later at line 248 with `power_supply_register(&dev->dev, &bat_ps);`.
